CHIEF COMPLAINT
Right leg pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mrs. Peterson is a 43-year-old female presenting with right upper leg pain. She reports the injury occurred while bowling. As she was running up to the lane with her bowling ball drawn back, she inadvertently struck her right leg with the ball instead of releasing it down the lane. She subsequently fell. The patient denies significant swelling but reports mild bruising on the posterior aspect of the leg. She has been able to walk only minimally and with great difficulty. She endorses significant pain with weight-bearing and states she would avoid stairs at all costs. She has been managing pain with alternating ibuprofen and acetaminophen.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Negative for systemic symptoms. Patient denies fever, chills, or constitutional symptoms.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Atopic eczema
2. Diverticulosis with prior diverticulitis, status post colectomy

MEDICATIONS
1. Fluocinonide - topical, used as needed for eczema when itchy
2. Ibuprofen - over the counter, alternating use
3. Acetaminophen (Tylenol) - over the counter, alternating use

ALLERGIES
Not documented.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient enjoys bowling.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Significant tenderness to palpation over the lateral aspect of the right upper leg. No pain or tenderness with flexion or extension of the lower leg. No evidence of significant swelling.

RESULTS
X-ray of right femur: Normal. No evidence of fracture or abnormal swelling.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Right leg contusion secondary to blunt trauma. Plan to initiate mobic 15 mg once daily for anti-inflammatory effect. Patient advised to use ice for pain management. Expect improvement within one week. Patient instructed to return if symptoms do not improve.
